title: 10. NLP, Transformers & LLMs: GloVe vs FastText: Advanced Word Embeddings
summary: Goal: Understand GloVe and FastText - improvements over Word2Vec.
objectives: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation

sections.title: Three Major Embedding Approaches
sections.body:
**Goal**: Understand GloVe and FastText - improvements over Word2Vec.

```
Word2Vec (2013)
├─ Local context window
├─ Predictive (CBOW/Skip-gram)
└─ Neural network training

GloVe (2014)
├─ Global co-occurrence statistics
├─ Matrix factorization
└─ Combines global + local info

FastText (2016)
├─ Subword information (character n-grams)
├─ Handles OOV words
└─ Morphologically aware
```

sections.title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation
sections.body:
### Key Idea

**Word2Vec**: Uses local context windows
```
"the cat sat on the mat"
     ↑   ↑   ↑
  Context window for "sat"
```

**GloVe**: Uses global word co-occurrence statistics
```
Co-occurrence Matrix (entire corpus):
         cat   dog   sat   mat   bark
cat      0     5     20    15    1
dog      5     0     18    3     25
sat      20    18    0     12    10
mat      15    3     12    0     2
bark     1     25    10    2     0

Key insight: cat & dog co-occur often → similar vectors
```

### Mathematical Intuition

**Objective**: Learn vectors such that their dot product equals log co-occurrence probability

$$
w_i^T w_j + b_i + b_j = \log(X_{ij})
$$

Where:
- $w_i, w_j$ = word vectors
- $b_i, b_j$ = bias terms
- $X_{ij}$ = co-occurrence count

**Loss Function**:
$$
J = \sum_{i,j=1}^{V} f(X_{ij})(w_i^T w_j + b_i + b_j - \log X_{ij})^2
$$

Where $f(X_{ij})$ is a weighting function that reduces influence of very common co-occurrences.

sections.title: GloVe vs Word2Vec
sections.body:
| Feature | Word2Vec | GloVe |
|---------|----------|-------|
| **Training** | Local context | Global statistics |
| **Method** | Neural network | Matrix factorization |
| **Speed** | Slower | Faster |
| **Memory** | Lower | Higher (co-occurrence matrix) |
| **Quality** | Very good | Very good |
| **Scalability** | Better | Good |

### When to Use Each

**Word2Vec**:
```
✓ Large streaming data
✓ Online/incremental learning
✓ Lower memory requirements
✓ Local context more important
```

**GloVe**:
```
✓ Fixed corpus
✓ Batch processing
✓ Global context matters
✓ Faster training (if fits in memory)
```

sections.title: FastText: Subword-Aware Embeddings
sections.body:
### The Problem Word2Vec/GloVe Can't Solve

```python
# Out-of-Vocabulary (OOV) words:
word = "amazingly"  # In vocabulary
word = "amazingly123"  # Not in vocabulary → Error!

# Morphological relations:
"teach" vs "teacher" vs "teaching"
→ Treated as completely different words!

# Typos:
"recieve" instead of "receive"
→ No embedding available!
```

### FastText Solution: Character N-grams

Break words into character n-grams:
```python
word = "where"
n=3 (trigrams):
  <wh, whe, her, ere, re>
  + special tokens: <where>

Final embedding = Sum of all n-gram embeddings
```

**Example**:
```
"teaching" = <te + tea + eac + ach + chi + hin + ing + ng>
            + <teaching> (whole word)

Even if "teaching" is OOV:
→ We can still compute embedding from character n-grams!
```

sections.title: FastText Advantages
sections.body:
### 1. Handles OOV Words

```python
# Word2Vec/GloVe:
model["amazingly"]     # ✓ Works
model["amazingly123"]  # ✗ KeyError!

# FastText:
model["amazingly"]     # ✓ Works
model["amazingly123"]  # ✓ Still works! (uses n-grams)
```

### 2. Morphological Awareness

```python
# FastText learns that these share n-grams:
"teach"    = <te+ea+ac+ch> + ...
"teacher"  = <te+ea+ac+ch+he+er> + ...
"teaching" = <te+ea+ac+ch+hi+in+ng> + ...

→ Similar embeddings automatically!
```

### 3. Handles Rare Words Better

```python
# Rare word with common subwords:
"neuroscientific" (may be rare)
= neuro + scientific (common components)
→ Good embedding even if word is rare!
```

### 4. Works with Typos

```python
# Common typo:
"recieve" (wrong spelling)
= <re+ec+ce+ei+iv+ve>
≈ "receive" (correct spelling)
= <re+ec+ce+ei+iv+ve>
→ Similar embeddings!
```

sections.title: Comparison Table
sections.body:
| Feature | Word2Vec | GloVe | FastText |
|---------|----------|-------|----------|
| **OOV Handling** | ✗ No | ✗ No | ✓ Yes |
| **Morphology** | ✗ Ignored | ✗ Ignored | ✓ Captured |
| **Training Speed** | Medium | Fast | Slower |
| **Memory** | Low | Medium | High |
| **File Size** | Medium | Medium | Large |
| **Rare Words** | Poor | Poor | Good |
| **Typos** | ✗ Fail | ✗ Fail | ✓ Handle |
| **Languages** | All | All | Better for morphologically rich |

sections.title: Which Embedding to Choose?
sections.body:
### Decision Tree

```
Do you have OOV words or typos?
├─ YES → Use FastText
└─ NO
    ├─ Fixed corpus, batch processing?
    │   └─ YES → Use GloVe
    └─ Streaming data, online learning?
        └─ YES → Use Word2Vec

Language morphologically rich (German, Finnish, Turkish)?
└─ YES → Strongly prefer FastText

Need smallest file size?
└─ YES → Use Word2Vec or GloVe

Need best quality for common words?
└─ Any of them work well!
```

sections.title: Pre-trained Models Available
sections.body:
### GloVe (Stanford)

```python
# Via gensim.downloader:
import gensim.downloader as api

# Wikipedia 2014 + Gigaword 5 (6B tokens, 400K vocab)
model = api.load('glove-wiki-gigaword-50')   # 65MB, 50d
model = api.load('glove-wiki-gigaword-100')  # 128MB, 100d
model = api.load('glove-wiki-gigaword-200')  # 252MB, 200d
model = api.load('glove-wiki-gigaword-300')  # 376MB, 300d

# Twitter (2B tweets, 1.2M vocab)
model = api.load('glove-twitter-25')   # 104MB, 25d
model = api.load('glove-twitter-50')   # 200MB, 50d
model = api.load('glove-twitter-100')  # 387MB, 100d
model = api.load('glove-twitter-200')  # 752MB, 200d

# Common Crawl (840B tokens, 2.2M vocab)
# Download from: https://nlp.stanford.edu/projects/glove/
# Files: 300d, 1.75GB
```

### FastText (Facebook)

```python
# Via gensim.downloader:
model = api.load('fasttext-wiki-news-subwords-300')  
# 1GB, 1M vocab, 300d, handles subwords!

# Via fasttext library:
import fasttext
import fasttext.util

# Download pre-trained models (157 languages!)
fasttext.util.download_model('en', if_exists='ignore')  # English
model = fasttext.load_model('cc.en.300.bin')

# Other languages:
fasttext.util.download_model('es')  # Spanish
fasttext.util.download_model('fr')  # French
fasttext.util.download_model('de')  # German
# ... 157 languages total!
```

sections.title: Use Cases
sections.body:
### GloVe is Best For:

```
✓ General-purpose NLP
✓ Sentiment analysis
✓ Text classification
✓ Document similarity
✓ When you have clean, well-formed text
✓ Wikipedia/news-style text
```

### FastText is Best For:

```
✓ Social media text (typos, slang)
✓ Domain-specific vocabulary (medical, legal)
✓ Morphologically rich languages
✓ Handling rare words
✓ Noisy text data
✓ When OOV is a problem
✓ Multilingual applications (157 languages!)
```

sections.title: Technical Details
sections.body:
### GloVe Training Steps:

1. **Build Co-occurrence Matrix**: Count word pairs within window
2. **Apply Weighting**: Down-weight very frequent co-occurrences
3. **Matrix Factorization**: Learn vectors that reconstruct matrix
4. **Optimize**: Minimize weighted squared error

### FastText Training Steps:

1. **Extract N-grams**: Break words into character n-grams (n=3-6)
2. **Assign Embeddings**: Each n-gram gets its own vector
3. **Word Embedding**: Sum of n-gram vectors + whole word vector
4. **Train**: Skip-gram objective like Word2Vec
5. **Inference**: For OOV word, just sum its n-gram vectors

sections.title: Performance Comparison
sections.body:
### Word Similarity Task (Spearman correlation):

| Model | WS-353 | SimLex-999 | RW |
|-------|---------|------------|-----|
| Word2Vec (300d) | 0.687 | 0.443 | 0.538 |
| GloVe (300d) | 0.623 | 0.404 | 0.478 |
| FastText (300d) | 0.658 | 0.442 | **0.571** |

### Word Analogy Task (Accuracy):

| Model | Semantic | Syntactic | Total |
|-------|----------|-----------|-------|
| Word2Vec (300d) | **74.2%** | 70.3% | **72.5%** |
| GloVe (300d) | 71.5% | 63.1% | 67.9% |
| FastText (300d) | 72.8% | **72.1%** | 72.5% |

### Key Takeaways:
- Word2Vec: Best for semantic analogies
- GloVe: Slightly lower but faster training
- FastText: Best for rare words and syntactic tasks

sections.title: Practical Recommendations
sections.body:
### For Production Systems:

**Start with**: GloVe 100d or 200d
```python
# Good balance of quality, speed, size
model = api.load('glove-wiki-gigaword-200')
```

**Upgrade to**: FastText if you encounter:
- Many OOV words (>5%)
- User-generated content (typos)
- Domain-specific vocabulary
- Morphologically rich language

**Use Word2Vec if**:
- You need online/incremental learning
- Streaming data
- Very large vocabulary

sections.title: Code Example Patterns
sections.body:
### GloVe Usage:
```python
import gensim.downloader as api

# Load
model = api.load('glove-wiki-gigaword-100')

# Use (same API as Word2Vec)
vec = model['computer']
similar = model.most_similar('computer', topn=5)
similarity = model.similarity('computer', 'laptop')
```

### FastText Usage:
```python
import fasttext
import fasttext.util

# Download and load
fasttext.util.download_model('en', if_exists='ignore')
model = fasttext.load_model('cc.en.300.bin')

# Get embedding (works for OOV!)
vec = model.get_word_vector('computer')
vec_oov = model.get_word_vector('amazingly123')  # ✓ Works!

# Find similar words
neighbors = model.get_nearest_neighbors('computer', k=5)
```

sections.title: Summary
sections.body:
### Choose GloVe When:
```
✓ Clean, well-formed text
✓ General-purpose NLP
✓ Want smaller file sizes
✓ Batch processing
✓ Don't need OOV handling
```

### Choose FastText When:
```
✓ Noisy text (social media)
✓ Need OOV handling
✓ Rare words are important
✓ Morphologically rich languages
✓ Typos and misspellings present
✓ 157 languages available!
```

### Choose Word2Vec When:
```
✓ Need incremental learning
✓ Streaming data
✓ Lower memory requirements
✓ Original implementation matters
```
